territorial_scope.description: Binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all EU Member States; the reporting templates cover Member State breakdowns.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

summary.short: Sets harmonised templates and formats for the content-moderation transparency reports that providers of intermediary services, hosting services and online platforms must publish under the Digital Services Act. Templates apply from 1 July 2025; reports are published within two months of each period and kept five years.
summary.long: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2835 lays down the templates, format and reporting periods for the transparency reports required by Articles 15, 24 and 42 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act). Providers of intermediary services, hosting services, online platforms, very large online platforms and very large online search engines must use the CSV or XLSX versions of the Annex I templates. The Quantitative Template covers Member State orders, notices, own-initiative content moderation, internal complaints, out-of-court dispute settlements, suspensions, use of automated means with accuracy indicators, moderator resources and monthly active recipients. The Qualitative Template requires descriptive information on content moderation and automated means. Annual reporting periods run from 1 January to 31 December for intermediary services, hosting services and online platforms, while very large online platforms and search engines report at least every six months. Reports must be made publicly available within two months after each reporting period ends, in machine-readable ODF CSV format in UTF-8, and retained publicly for at least five years. Templates apply as of 1 July 2025, with transition rules for the 2025 reporting cycles set out in Annex II. Updated versions of reports must be clearly marked.

thresholds.note: This implementing regulation sets report templates, timelines and retention periods; it contains no numeric cutoffs that change legal treatment in its operative provisions. The micro/small enterprise exemption (Art. 15(2)) and the VLOP designation (Art. 33) are referenced only in recitals or in Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, which is not part of this text. Time periods and report-count fields are coded as deadlines or reporting items, not thresholds.
